newsitem.title: FRANCE: Truckers' strike gets critical - Air France.
newsitem.headline: Truckers' strike gets critical - Air France.

text.p: Air France Cargo said on Tuesday a critical situation could develop for trucked airfreight if there were not a speedy settlement to the French lorry drivers dispute.

"As far as we're concerned the situation has become difficult with services running behind schedule. However, we have not yet reached crisis point which could be the case if the dispute was prolonged," an airline official told Reuters.

The fact that lorry drivers had lifted a barricade near Paris/Charles de Gaulle airport at 18.00 local (17.00 GMT) on Monday had enabled Air France trucks to leave as scheduled for destinations in France and Europe, the official said.
The airline's trucking services were hardest-hit around Bordeaux, the Franco-Spanish and Franco-German borders, Calais and Dover, the official added.
Around 75 percent of Air France's overall cargo volumes handled at the Paris airports are accounted for by non-French freight in transit.
This traffic has either originated from or is destined for a country other than France, so the airline's European trucking network plays an integral role in the forwarding and re-forwarding of cargo.
A CDG-based forwarder said it had cancelled its twice-daily trucking shuttle service between Paris and Lyon on Tuesday because of the road barricades.

"Roads in most regions are affected, particularly in eastern France, where we have vehicles stuck in traffic en route to Frankfurt. Some in-bound freight to CDG this evening just won't arrive in time to make flight connections," the firm said.
